metadata.description: Alex's personal Claude Code plugin marketplace.

plugins.name: browser-lab
plugins.description: The live-browser toolkit: browser automation, deep frontend debugging, network disassembly, and HTTP request replication. Routes every task across Playwright, Chrome DevTools, and mitmproxy. For retrieval, install web-harvest.

plugins.name: web-harvest
plugins.description: The retrieval router for the open web: search, scrape, crawl, and structured extraction at scale across Firecrawl, Exa, Tavily, Bright Data, and Apify, with cost-aware escalation. All five backends are hosted HTTP connectors, so it holds no local process.

plugins.name: agents-os
plugins.description: Operating knowledge for the personal Agentic OS. The hetzner-server skill covers the VPS that runs every agent: where its current state actually lives, which commands are safe, and what has to be updated after a change so the next session is not reading a stale document.

plugins.name: alex-git
plugins.description: The map of Alex's git estate: every working copy and its remote, which GitHub identity actually pushes and what its token may not do, what a push to a given branch deploys, and the traps already paid for once — a 'Repository not found' that is really a blocked transport, work hiding in a second clone, and the two-way Shopify theme sync.

plugins.name: design-pipeline
plugins.description: The conveyor: builds a complete web surface end-to-end through ten gates, each owned by one vendor skill and each closing on a checkable artifact — intake, brief, tokens, references, art direction, wireframe, build, states, motion, SEO/CWV/a11y audit, ship verdict. Wraps ui-craft's phase commands rather than re-implementing them, and closes the four holes ui-craft leaves: intake, visual references, isolated art direction, and search/performance audit. For single-aspect passes on existing UI, install design-tools.

plugins.name: design-tools
plugins.description: The router: one targeted design pass on UI that already exists. Reads the request in the user's own words, picks exactly one specialist skill out of eighty-seven across ui-craft, taste-skill, impeccable, Emil Kowalski, Addy Osmani's web-quality suite, ibelick and nine smaller vendors — then resolves where that skill is actually installed and loads it, so the route works from any project, not only design-studio. Carries what no single vendor has: a collision table for the twelve places where three vendors cover the same ground, read-only-before-write discipline, a hard escalation threshold to design-pipeline, a registry-driven wiki of every vendor and tool, one vendor-prefixed command per tool (/design-tools:ui-craft-typeset, /design-tools:osmani-seo, …) so the picker groups them, and one entry command per vendor (/design-tools:ui-craft, /design-tools:impeccable, /design-tools:taste) that runs the vendor's master skill exactly as the vendor designed it.
